transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess I'm here because the regular clinic doctor got on my case about my eating. 

I don't really see the big deal, honestly. Most days I just keep it pretty simple. I'll have coffee in the morning, maybe grab a few bites of something between painting jobs, and then just a small dinner if I'm not too bogged down with my class paperwork. It's just what works for my schedule.
When you eat less than usual, is it mainly because you're busy, or are you also trying to control your weight or shape?

It's a bit of both, honestly. I mean, I am busy, but... yeah, I am trying to keep my weight down. 

If I eat something heavy, like a big sandwich or pizza, I actually get this panicky feeling. I just start thinking that I'll wake up bigger and slower. I'm up and down ladders all day for work, reaching and bending in tight spaces, and I just worry that I won't be able to move around the ladders and rooms the way I need to if I put on weight. So it's easier to just avoid it.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and whether you've lost weight recently?

I'm about 5'6", and... well, I haven't stepped on a scale in a little while, but I think I'm around 105 pounds right now. 

I guess I have lost some weight recently. My work pants hang pretty loose on me now. A lot of the guys on the job sites keep saying I look too thin, but honestly, I just see it more like I've leaned out from staying on my feet all day.
When you look in the mirror at your current weight, do you feel that you look too thin, about right, or still not thin enough?

Honestly, when I look in the mirror, I think I look about right. I definitely don't see myself as too thin. 

I don't really think my weight is some emergency like everyone keeps acting. To me, it just feels like they're making a huge deal out of me being disciplined and staying busy with my jobs. I'm just doing what I need to do to keep working, so I don't really get what the fuss is about.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient demonstrates significant low body weight (BMI ~16.9, calculated from self-reported height/weight), intentional caloric restriction driven by intense fear of weight gain and impaired mobility, and a persistent distortion of body image (perceiving self as 'about right' despite being visibly underweight per collateral observation from coworkers and clinician concern). There is minimization/denial of the seriousness of low weight, and no reported binge-eating or purging behaviors, consistent with Anorexia Nervosa, restricting-type presentation (F50.0). Differential includes atypical anorexia nervosa (F50.1) if strict weight/BMI thresholds are not fully met, and unspecified eating disorder (F50.9) if further clarification of duration/amenorrhea or other criteria is needed.
